standard_prerequisites.name: Contravariance of Hom in its first variable

standard_prerequisites.use: Turns a surjection onto M into an inclusion of the Hom module into the product, which is the whole argument.

core_obligations: Choose a surjection from a direct sum of copies of R onto M (proof line 5002).
Apply Hom_R(-, N) to that surjection to get an injection Hom_R(M, N) into the product of copies of N indexed by the same set (proof lines 5002-5003).
Use the torsion freeness of N and the elementwise nature of torsion to conclude that the submodule Hom_R(M, N) is torsion free (proof lines 5003-5004).
proof_roadmap: Interval comparison against the 57 public records of more-algebra.tex: no recorded interval covers 4995-5004. The nearest records are 336 (4721-4764, tag 0H7R) and 337 (5577-5633, tag 0AVB); public 337 is about reflexive modules, which are defined by a comparison of a module with its double dual, so it does touch Hom functors, but it proves statements about codimension-one intersections rather than the torsion freeness of Hom_R(M, N).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that Hom_R(M, N) is torsion free whenever N is, for arbitrary modules over a domain, and the author's proof is a two-line containment argument (statement lines 4995-4998, proof lines 5001-5004). It chooses a surjection from a direct sum of copies of R onto M and uses it to realise Hom_R(M, N) as a submodule of a product of copies of N (proof lines 5002-5003). The non-formal content is the choice of presentation and the direction of the induced map: the surjection on the first variable of Hom gives an injection into the product with Man itself, whereas the opposite arrow would be the wrong way. The reader also has to notice that the assertion is about torsion elements, which are tested elementwise, so a submodule of a product of torsion free modules is again torsion free.
